text: CHAPTER 27
speaker: Narrator

text: The Man Who Refused
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: They did not return to the plaza.
speaker: Narrator

text: The knocking faded after a time, as if the City had noted their refusal and simply transferred the account to a later column. The three paving stones looked ordinary again. Only the erased names on the lintels remained as proof that someone had once answered when asked.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag kept his hand on Zik's shoulder until they were well clear of the unfinished street.
speaker: Narrator

text: Next time you test a threshold,
speaker: Balag

text: he said,
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: you say so first.
speaker: Balag

text: Zik nodded. He still tasted the shape of his own full name at the back of his throat.
speaker: Narrator

text: Enhedu glanced back once at the blank floor.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: We still don't know what happens if someone actually pays.
speaker: Enhedu

text: We know enough,
speaker: Ninsun

text: Ninsun answered. She was writing again, stylus moving in short, precise strokes.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: That distinction survives in every damaged tablet that still mentions the gates.
speaker: Ninsun

text: They chose a narrower street that at least possessed two walls and a visible far end. The geometry continued to refuse ordinary rules. A covered walkway they passed beneath reappeared ahead of them a short while later, identical down to one cracked tile. Zik stopped leaving trail markers. There was no longer any point.
speaker: Narrator

text: The deeper they went, the more traces of ordinary life surfaced—and the more wrong those traces felt. A market stall carved directly into a building's side still held the faint outlines of jars that no longer existed. A child's handprint was pressed into a wall at waist height, the fingers too small, the impression too deep. Doorways showed thresholds worn smooth by generations of feet, yet their upper lintels remained sharp, as if the people who lived here had eventually stopped looking up.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun slowed beside a low wall covered in faint wedge-shaped marks. She brushed dust away with careful fingers.
speaker: Narrator

text: Inventory,
speaker: Ninsun

text: she said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Grain. Oil. Rope. The same lists every household kept.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Near the bottom three lines had been crossed out so thoroughly the surface beneath was scraped raw. Beside the erasure someone had later cut a single incomplete spiral.
speaker: Narrator

text: They inventoried people,
speaker: Ninsun

text: she said quietly.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: No one asked her to continue.
speaker: Narrator

text: The street narrowed further. Torchlight sank into the oily stone and did not return. Somewhere ahead, water dripped with the slow regularity of a clock that no longer measured hours anyone recognized.
speaker: Narrator

text: Then they heard the voice.
speaker: Narrator

text: It was thin, human, and exhausted, and it came from a side passage so narrow they would have walked past it without noticing.
speaker: Narrator

text: Don't give it your name.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: Balag's axe was up before the last word finished. Enhedu had already angled herself for a fight. Ninsun froze with the stylus still pressed to parchment.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik raised the torch.
speaker: Narrator

text: The passage ended after only a few paces in a shallow alcove. A man sat against the back wall, knees drawn up, wrists resting loosely on them. His clothes were the same dust-fused linen they had seen on the gatekeeper, but his skin was still skin—gray, stretched thin, cracked at the corners of the mouth. His eyes tracked the torchlight with the slow recognition of someone who had not expected living faces again.
speaker: Narrator

text: You're real,
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: the man said. His voice sounded unused.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I thought the City had finally learned how to make better copies.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: Zik crouched just out of reach.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Who are you?
speaker: Zik

text: The man gave a one-sided smile.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: That depends which name you're asking for. The one I arrived with, or the one it left me.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: Ninsun's stylus hovered.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: How long have you been here?
speaker: Ninsun

text: I stopped counting after the second winter that never ended.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: He looked past them toward the main street.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: You're still carrying your names. That's rarer than it should be. Most who reach this depth have already paid at least once.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: Balag kept the axe ready.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Are there others?
speaker: Balag

text: There were.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: The man lifted one thin hand and pointed farther down the narrowing street.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The City keeps what it collects. Sometimes it lets the emptier ones walk for a while. Sometimes it uses them as markers. Sometimes it just leaves them where they fall.
speaker: The Man Who Refused

text: Enhedu studied him the way she studied anything that might still hold value.
speaker: Narrator
